title: Parables of Recognition
claim: The teaching is older than its treatises: thirty-six original parables, each with a full-page drawing, carry the recognition of the whole in the plain speech of a story — not a verse commentary but a door for a reader who will never open a śāstra.

purpose.impact: Thirty-six stories that do the work a treatise cannot: the reader recognises themselves in the third person and laughs before the point lands.
purpose.reader: The reader who will never open a śāstra, and the practitioner who has read too many.
purpose.realisation: The teaching is not information but a turn of the story — the reader sees the knot from outside and finds they were holding it.
non_goals: no verse citation or one-to-one mapping to a text
no final art without owner signoff

pages.note: 36 stories as spreads (72pp) + front 10 + glossary 8 + index 6 + end 4 = 100, padded to 108.

sections_plan.purpose: stories of misidentification and the sense of lack
stories of the self met as another
stories of the ordinary world as the temple
stories of reflection, image and recognition
stories of transmission and the word
stories of language, mantra and naming
stories of seeing and being seen
stories of action, work and desire
stories of the ordinary after recognition
